title: Tuesday Quick Tip
subtitle: When a player freezes
hook: A player who is great in practice disappears in games.
intro: In practice, they field every grounder.
In games, they freeze and hope it is not hit to them.
statement: Freezing is usually nerves, not a lack of skill.
q1: Do you give that player one simple job in games —
q2: or let them play and grow into it?
q3: What makes games feel different to them?
t1: There is no single right way. But nervous players settle
t2: when they know exactly what to do first.
cta: Coaches — how do you help a frozen player?
ctaLines: One job. One early ground ball. A calm word.
A simple role or time to adjust?
ctaPrompt: Share your habit below. There are no wrong answers.
caption:
A player who is great in practice disappears in games.
In practice, they field every grounder. In games, they freeze and hope it is not hit to them.
Freezing is usually nerves, not a lack of skill.
A simple job or time to grow into it. Both can work.
How do you help a frozen player? Share your habit in the comments.
